newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent crude closes firmer on Iraq, technicals.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent crude closes firmer on Iraq, technicals.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil futures closed firmer on Tuesday after a thin session of choppy trading influenced by news out of Iraq and technical chart factors, brokers said.
October Brent closed 27 cents a barrel up on the day at $22.88 after breaking through a five-month high at $22.85.
"It is very frothy and very thin," said Charles Gray of Prudential-Bache in London.
"Traders are getting spooked on any sort of story."
The U.S. government denied Iraq's claim that it had fired three missiles at U.S. aircraft in the southern no-fly zone.
"We have absolutely no indication of that," a U.S. spokesman said in response to the claims.
Another U.S. spokesman added: "We have warned Saddam Hussein that we retain the right and will, in fact, take actions necessary to protect our pilots. And we will do that."
Brent had jumped nearly 20 cents on news of the alleged attack before settling back after the U.S. denial.
Dealers watching the technical price charts said the market's failure in the morning to break below Monday's $22.31 low had signalled an upwards move.
This was then reinforced by U.S. markets which quickly moved higher and broke through an important psychological resistance level on the October contract at $24.00.

October NYMEX was trading at $24.12 at 1930 GMT and traders said the transatlantic arbitrage differential between the October crude contracts had widened to around $1.25 a barrel, compared with $1.10 to $1.15 on Monday.
September IPE gas oil earlier closed 75 cents firmer at $217.75 a tonne. The strength in the energy complex dragged gas oil higher despite news of physical cargoes sailing eastwards into Europe.
IPE brokers said that the expiry of the October Brent contract on Friday, and the expiry of September gas oil on Thursday, had increased the volatility of both contracts.
